findings.description: discounts=[] is a shared default list, and line 15 appends BULK_DISCOUNT to it, so the discount accumulates across calls and persists for the life of the process.
findings.scenario: Call invoice_total with 11 items twice with no discounts argument: the second call applies 5% twice (list is [0.05, 0.05]). A later call with 1 item still gets the leftover 5% discount.
findings.fix: def invoice_total(items, discounts=None): discounts = list(discounts or []); then append to the local copy.

findings.description: datetime.now() returns a naive local datetime, but due_at is timezone-aware UTC. Comparing them raises TypeError.
findings.scenario: is_overdue({'due_at': datetime(2026,1,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc)}) raises TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes.

findings.description: Tax is computed with float arithmetic and Python's banker's-style round() on a float, and the total is returned as float, contradicting the Decimal-dollars contract. Discounted subtotal is also never quantized to cents.
findings.scenario: Subtotal of 10.00 with tax 0.0825 gives 0.825; float round(...) may yield 0.82 instead of 0.83 (ROUND_HALF_UP expected), and sums can drift by a cent.
findings.fix: Use Decimal: subtotal = subtotal.quantize(Decimal('0.01'), ROUND_HALF_UP); tax = (subtotal * Decimal('0.0825')).quantize(Decimal('0.01'), ROUND_HALF_UP); return subtotal + tax.

findings.description: Uses len(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD, so exactly 10 items gets no discount; a constant named threshold is often read as inclusive. Also counts line items, not quantity.
findings.scenario: An invoice with exactly 10 lines gets no bulk discount if the intent was 10 or more.
findings.fix: Confirm intended semantics; if inclusive use >=, and document it.
